newsitem.title: JAPAN: TIFFE Euroyen end down on Kajiyama comments.
newsitem.headline: TIFFE Euroyen end down on Kajiyama comments.

text.p: The key December three-month Euroyen futures contract ended slightly down on Wednesday due to a senior Japanese government official's comments on interest rates, traders said.

Chief government spokesman Seiroku Kajiyama told a parliamentary budget committee meeting on Wednesday that Japan needs to consider measures to deal with the adverse impact low interest rates have on people's incomes.

"The only thing Japan can be proud of in the rough wave of internationalisation is its extra-low interest rates. On the other hand, it means Japan lags behind in internationalisation. I think in the near future Japan will undergo rough waves and I think it is necessary to consider measures to cope with that." Kajiyama said.
He made the remarks in response to a question about the effect Japan's low interest rates had on people's incomes.
A U.S. brokerage house apparently sold 1,000 contracts of the June Euroyen futures contract on SIMEX, a trader for a European brokerage house said.
A U.S. hedge fund was probably behind the selling, which took place at 99.39, the trader said.
Traders said foreign financial institutions have been taking a bearish stance on euroyen futures recently.
"Foreign market players have been biased toward building short positions recently. They seem to feel that euroyen futures are heavy on the upperside," a city bank trader said.
The trader said, however, he felt the December's downside was limited, with support at 99.16 or 99.15 in the near term.
The Bank of Japan injected a net 300 billion yen into the money market this morning, maintaining it accommodative stance.
The BOJ's operation came against a fund shortage of 190 billion yen.

The key overnight call rate's weighted average is likely to be 0.49 percent on Wednesday, unchanged from the previous day, traders said. They said some city banks' recent preference for borrowing short-term funds was keeping the overnight call rate stuck near 0.50 percent.
Traders said the BOJ will probably maintain its accommodative stance at least through the end of the week.
About 50 billion yen worth of the key three-month certificates of deposit were issued at 0.54 percent.
